concepts.title: Continental Drift Theory of Wegener
concepts.definition: Alfred Wegener's continental drift theory proposed that all continents formed a single landmass Pangaea surrounded by the ocean Panthalassa, which broke into Laurasia and Gondwanaland and drifted apart, supported by jigsaw fit of continents, rocks of same age, tillite deposits, placer deposits and fossil evidence.
concepts.key_idea: Wegener suggested pole-fleeing tidal and gravitational differential forces for drift, but the theory failed to explain the driving force until sea floor spreading revived it.

concepts.title: Sea Floor Spreading and Plate Tectonics
concepts.definition: Harry Hess's sea floor spreading showed new crust forming at mid-ocean ridges and sinking at trenches, and plate tectonics divides the lithosphere into seven major plates moving over the asthenosphere, with divergent, convergent and transform boundaries building mountains, trenches and volcanoes.
concepts.key_idea: Convergent boundaries of ocean-continent, continent-continent and ocean-ocean type produce Andes, Himalayas and island arcs respectively, explaining the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes.

concepts.title: Distribution of Oceans, Continents and Indian Plate Movements
concepts.definition: Oceans cover about 71 per cent and continents about 29 per cent of the earth's surface, and the Indian plate's northward drift after breaking from Gondwanaland continues to push the Himalayas upward while making the Indian subcontinent seismically active.
concepts.key_idea: The distribution of land and water follows plate boundaries, with mid ocean ridges marking construction and trenches marking consumption of crust.
